raw: 13.2 APT Risk Propagation Models: ATT&CK-Based Analysis[^72]
teaching_note: A propagation graph proposes possible dependencies; its edges are not observed causal transitions merely because nodes carry ATT&CK labels. Any calculated risk depends on the model's assumptions, input probabilities and validation population, none of which is supplied by a title or abstract alone. Compare a hypothetical edge with a supplied record that could falsify it, and report model-scoped outputs separately from empirical intrusion likelihood.
title: APT Risk Propagation Models: ATT&CK-Based Analysis

raw: 13.3 Nation-State vs. Ideological Actor Attack Patterns[^69]
teaching_note: State sponsorship and ideological motivation are not mutually exclusive classes, and financially motivated contractors can complicate both labels. Shared tools, working hours and target sectors are compatible with multiple explanations and do not identify nationality or motive. The inherited study reference cannot support categorical differences without its inspected sampling and attribution criteria; this chapter makes no quantitative superiority or prevalence claim.
title: Nation-State vs. Ideological Actor Attack Patterns

raw: 13.4 APT Infrastructure: C2 Frameworks, Domain Fronting, Bulletproof Hosting

Shared hosting, reassignment and reused software can explain overlap without common control. title: Incident-Record Review: Limits of the Inherited Mandiant Methodology Claim

teaching_note: A hunt hypothesis predicts a discriminating observation; a hit is a candidate record, not a malicious-actor finding. In a fictional offline packet, event E1 records inventory enumeration at 09:00, approved task card C1 schedules that enumeration at 09:00, duplicate feed E2 copies E1, and coverage card K1 says authentication records for 08:00–10:00 are absent. Comparison yields 'observed enumeration consistent with approved task; adversarial mapping unestablished', with one event lineage rather than two hits; removing C1 makes purpose unknown, not malicious. K1 prevents interpreting no authentication hits as no intrusion, and a high hypothetical impact rating would not increase attribution confidence or telemetry coverage. The attached AI/supply-chain sources are not evidence for a hunt's accuracy; no commands, scans, malware, blocking or live response are used.
title: Threat Hunting Against APT Actors

raw: 13.7 APT Attribution: Technical Indicators vs. Geopolitical Context
teaching_note: In a completed synthetic case, reports A and B repeat source S's claim that campaign X used artifact H; record C shows H was publicly shared before X, and no record links H to an operator. Collapsing A/B to one origin and testing the shared-tool alternative yields 'artifact overlap reported; operator and sponsor unknown', not attribution from two reports. Removing S eliminates the overlap claim, while adding C weakens H's discriminating value; stop before naming an actor and update if S retracts its claim. STIX can encode the competing assertions and TAXII can transport them, but those standards and ATLAS do not adjudicate factual attribution [@ageint309; @ageint310; @ageint300].
title: APT Attribution: Technical Indicators vs. Geopolitical Context
